# jenkins_credential_oidc_id_token (Resource)

Manages an OpenID Connect id token credential within Jenkins. Binding the credential in a build (for example with `withCredentials([string(...)])`) yields a short-lived id token signed by Jenkins, which the build can exchange with an external service that trusts Jenkins as an OpenID Connect issuer.

Jenkins generates the RSA signing key when the credential is created, and the key never leaves Jenkins or enters Terraform state.

~> Jenkins generates a new signing key whenever this credential is saved, so every argument forces replacement. A service that reads the JSON Web Key Set from Jenkins picks the new key up by itself. With a custom `issuer` you host that document yourself, and must publish it again after each replacement.

~> The Jenkins installation that uses this resource is expected to have the [OpenID Connect Provider Plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/oidc-provider/) installed in their system. The plugin only issues tokens for credentials in the global domain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jenkins_credential_oidc_id_token" "example" {
  name     = "example-id-token"
  audience = "https://service.example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the resource being created. This maps to the ID property within Jenkins, and cannot be changed once set.

### Optional

- `audience` (String) The audience (`aud`) claim of the id token, as expected by the service that verifies it.
- `description` (String) A human readable description of the credentials being stored.
- `domain` (String) The domain store to place the credentials into. If not set will default to the global credentials store.
- `folder` (String) The folder namespace to store the resource in. If not set will default to global Jenkins.
- `issuer` (String) The issuer (`iss`) claim of the id token. If not set, Jenkins uses its own issuer URI (`<jenkins-url>/oidc`, or `<jenkins-url>/oidc/job/<folder>` for a folder credential) and serves the discovery documents there; `effective_issuer` reports it. Set this only when you host the discovery documents yourself at an `https` URI.
- `scope` (String) The visibility of the credentials to Jenkins agents. This must be set to either "GLOBAL" or "SYSTEM". If not set will default to "GLOBAL".

### Read-Only

- `effective_issuer` (String) The issuer (`iss`) claim that tokens from this credential carry: `issuer` when it is set, otherwise the issuer URI Jenkins reports for the credential's store. It is built from the Jenkins URL configured in Jenkins, which may differ from the provider's `server_url`. Register this value with the service that verifies the tokens.
- `id` (String) The full canonical job path, e.g. `/job/job-name`
